svg.title: JavaScript 1.9 - Event Loop and Scheduling
svg.desc: Call stack, task sources, microtask checkpoints, timers and animation frames.
svg.text: Print-first interview refresher | execution → queues → rendering opportunities

g.text: 1 | Readiness does not interrupt a running call
Call stack
ordinary calls run to completion
Host environment
timers / network / input
Ready callback
wait for its scheduling boundary
A zero-delay timer does not run inline. A synchronous callback is not a new task.
Browsers have multiple task sources; no universal FIFO order across input, timers and network.
2 | Microtask checkpoint: drain, including newly queued work
Ready Promise reactions and queueMicrotask follow enqueue order; no fixed Promise-first rule.
Promise executor: synchronous. A reaction on a pending promise is not ready yet.
sync → end → promise → micro → nested → timer
If promise adds nested while micro already waits, nested joins the tail.
A timer callback can queue a microtask that runs before the next timer callback.
3 | An empty stack is not enough if the checkpoint never ends
Recursive microtasks
No growing stack, but tasks can starve.
Awaiting ready promises is not a UI yield.
Bounded chunks in ordinary tasks
Return control between short batches.
One costly item can still block the thread.
Create a scheduling opportunity, not a promise that every intermediate state will be painted.
4 | Timers: eligibility threshold, not an appointment
Busy JavaScript, other tasks and background policy can delay delivery.
Nested timer level > 5 and delay < 4 ms: raise the delay to 4 ms; not an exact 4 ms period.
Count time from a deadline, not from the number of interval callbacks.
remaining seconds = max(0, ceil((deadline - now) / 1000)) | use compatible clocks
5 | requestAnimationFrame: one visual callback, then request again
Use its timestamp: position = speed × elapsed time. Do not add fixed pixels per frame.
Coalesce updates: latest value + at most one pending frame; clear the ID before applying.
Cancel the pending frame on disposal. Hidden pages may pause animation callbacks.
A long callback delays rendering. rAF is not an after-paint notification.
6 | Predict causes, verify the contract
Name the runtime → execute sync code → enqueue only ready work → drain microtasks.
Continue with permitted tasks and frame work; keep unspecified cross-source order partial.
Test cancellation, empty input, reentrant updates and independent owners.
Use controlled timestamps for math and real browser APIs for lifecycle; avoid exact milliseconds.

svg.text: Rendering is not guaranteed after every task
DOM state, layout and displayed pixels are different. Node.js has its own host scheduling model.
